issue_context.title: Reduce duplicated code in IInheritable
issue_context.body: Follow-up from #9079. In `IInheritable.h`, `_get##name##OverrideSourceImpl` and `_get##name##Impl` are both very similar. We can reduce duplicated code by implementing the parent walking in the base class.

review_comments: That's a reserved identifier. (But it's fine.)
This might be wrong. I need to investigate.
I forgot that `NullableSetting` was a typedef for `opt<opt<T>>`. This is fine.

I'd personally just write `storageType _##name`, but I don't mind this either.

On the other hand we now need to be careful about these things now, because cppwinrt is being weird and allocates stuff in what is basically a "com_ptr". 😅
If you want `com_ptr` behavior, you use `com_ptr`. I might understand why they made the smart wrapper types allocate by default, but regardless, they are no longer "basically a com_ptr". 😉

Specifically what I meant is that _all_ stdlib classes which are nullable or "emptyable" (string, vector, etc., unique_ptr, shared_ptr, etc. and most importantly: std::optional) are all empty by default. It feels very weird to me that a nullable type's default constructor creates a non-null instance. (I get why it's that way though.)
It makes me wary of recommending people to just use the default constructor of types...
